IRL: safety that expands your world. A privacy-focused safety app designed with women at the centre, built in phases as a final-year B.Tech project. Safe enough to live. Free enough to grow.
This build has real accounts (sign-in with your mobile number and a texted code; no password, no e-mail), a Safety Circle, a manual SOS session, Safe Walk with check-ins and movement checks. Nobody can use IRL to track another person. During SOS or a Safe Walk, your location can be saved to your own records. Your Safety Circle is texted from your phone only if you switch on automatic SMS. IRL never contacts emergency services and never records sound, photos or video during an SOS.
The order of posts on Home uses what a post contains and the interests you chose; \"Talking now\" uses how recently someone commented. It never uses how many people read or commented.

IRL is a student prototype, not a released product, and there are no final terms of use yet. It is not an emergency service: it never contacts the police, an ambulance or anyone else for you, and an SMS that was sent is not proof that it was delivered or read. In an emergency, call 112 or your local emergency number. Do not rely on IRL as your only way to get help. Terms of use will be written and reviewed before any public release.

Privacy notice for this prototype build. It describes what this build actually does. It is written by the project team, is not legal advice and is not a final privacy policy.
Who can see your data: you, and the people who run the IRL server (the project team). Nobody else can look you up, follow you or see where you are: IRL has no family, partner or guardian mode, no location on request and no remote view, by design. IRL has no advertising and no analytics, and does not read your phone\'s contacts or messages.
Account: you sign in with your mobile number and a 6-digit code texted to it; there is no password and no e-mail. The server stores your real name, your number and when you confirmed that you are 18 or older (your date of birth is checked once and never stored). Codes are kept on the server only as a one-way hash for a few minutes; wrong codes and requests are counted in the server\'s memory only. This device stores your name, the last 4 digits of your number and a sign-in token, sealed with a key held by your phone\'s secure hardware. Deleting your account, cancelling that, signing out your other phones and ending an SOS from another phone are confirmed with a fresh code texted to your number. Asking to delete your account starts a 7-day wait; after it, everything your account holds on the server is deleted (see the end of this notice).
Location: only while an emergency is active, and only if you allow it, your phone\'s location (with its accuracy and the battery level) is saved to your own emergency record on the IRL server. Only you can see the saved points; the only place your location goes beyond that is a map link in the Safety Circle SMS, and only if you switch on automatic SMS or send it yourself (see below). Points that are waiting to be uploaded are kept in memory, not stored on the phone. Location points are deleted together with the emergency record and your account.
SOS without internet: an SOS starts on your phone at once, even without a connection, and is recorded on the server as soon as it can be reached. Until then the phone keeps only a random reference for the SOS, its start and end times and whether you tapped Call 112 (no location, no number); the server stores the reference and marks the times as your phone\'s. Signing out deletes what is still waiting.
Safe Walk: the server stores the walk (optional destination text you type, check-in times, missed check-ins) and only the LATEST location of your phone during the walk, which replaces the previous one. No route or track is kept. Nobody is contacted unless you switch on automatic SMS (see below).
Stop and route checks (if switched on): the destination text you type is looked up with your phone\'s map service (Google on most phones) and its coordinates are stored with the walk. Your phone compares its position with the direct route in memory only; no movement history is stored on the phone or the server. When a walk ends normally, its destination coordinates and last location are deleted from the server; if it ended in an emergency they are kept with that walk.
Safety Circle SMS (only if you switch on automatic SMS, or when you tap Text yourself): your phone sends an SMS to your enabled contacts with your name, the time, what happened and a map link to your last location. To work without internet, your enabled contacts\' names and numbers are kept on this phone (deleted when you log out). The server records only that a message was sent, to which contact and its status; never the number or the text. Tapping Call 112 opens your phone\'s dialer; IRL records that it was opened, not whether you called.
Account deletion: you confirm it with a code texted to your number; it is refused during an emergency and for 24 hours after one, and it waits 7 days (cancel with a code; signing in does not cancel it). Then the server deletes your account and everything it holds: emergencies and their locations, walks and Safety Circle. If you ever acted as a moderator, your account row stays as an anonymous, switched-off record so that the moderation log keeps who decided what; your name, number and safety data are still deleted. After the deletion, this phone removes the settings it kept for the account the next time it learns of it, or when you tap the button on the login screen.
Retention in short: emergency locations and walks stay until you delete them or your account; walk destinations and last locations are deleted when a walk ends normally; moderation log 365 days.
A complete privacy policy will be written and reviewed before any public release.

• Anyone can report a post, a comment or a person. Nobody is told who reported.
• When several people report something on their own, it is shown collapsed, behind a tap, until a moderator from the team looks at it.
• Only a moderator can hide or remove something, or pause someone, and always with a reason you can see.
• You can ask for a review of a decision. Another moderator looks at it.
• Moderation never touches your SOS or your other safety tools: walks with check-ins, the Safety Circle and the Evidence Vault.

An optional way to make an SOS quicker. It is off until you turn it on, and you can change it any time.

Shake the phone firmly three times and the same 5-second SOS countdown starts. You can cancel it. A shake never sends anything by itself. It works while IRL is open. During a Safe Walk it also tries with the screen off (the countdown is then a notification with a Cancel button), but many phones pause their motion sensor when the screen is off, so do not rely on shaking then. The SOS button, the Quick Settings tile and the launcher shortcut always work.
This phone has no motion sensor, so shaking cannot be used.
Notifications are off, so shaking works only while IRL is open. During a Safe Walk with the screen off there would be no way to cancel the countdown.

Starting an SOS by voice is not available. A phone cannot reliably keep listening in the background, and it would mean a microphone that is always on. The SOS button, the Quick Settings tile, the launcher shortcut and (if you turn it on) shaking are the ways to start one.
